title: Krishna Returns to Mathura
one_line_summary: Rama and Krishna, accompanied by Damaghosha, enter Mathura and are received with joy by Ugrasena and the Yadavas before honoring their parents.
source_excerpt: Thereupon seated on a car drawn by beautiful horses Rāma and Keshava entered the city of Mathurā in an auspicious moment. ... they entered into the house of their sire Vasudeva. ... bowing unto the feet of Vasudeva they showed proper honor to king Ugrasena and other leading Yadavas.

title: Balarama Revisits Vraja
one_line_summary: Balarama returns alone to Vraja, is welcomed by the cowherds, and sports with the gopis and drinks wine in the forest.
source_excerpt: After some days had thus elapsed, Rāma, recollecting his friendship with Gopas, alone went to Vraja with Krishna's consent. ... 'We had been reared by you and spent our boyhood in sporting here. We took our meals in your houses and tended the kine.'

title: Balarama Drags the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Inebriated Balarama summons the river Yamuna, and when she ignores him, he drags her out of her course with his ploughshare until she takes a woman's form and begs his pardon.
source_excerpt: Thereupon Rāma said to Yamunā:—'O great river, going to the ocean, I wish to marry you by bathing in your water; come to me therefore in your bodily form.' ... Dragged with force by Rāma the powerful river Yamunā ... began to follow the way pointed out by the plough-share.

title: News of Rukmini's Swayamvara
one_line_summary: Spies inform Krishna that Rukmini, sister of Rukmi, will hold her swayamvara at Kundina; Krishna sets out with the Yadava army, bidding Ugrasena guard Mathura.
source_excerpt: the emissaries announced ... 'Rukshmini, the first sister of Rukshmi, will hold her Swayamvara.' ... Keshava, the foremost of Yadus, set out immediately with his army.

title: Krishna Summons Garuda
one_line_summary: Arriving at Bhishmaka's house for the swayamvara, Krishna thinks of Garuda to overawe the assembled kings, and the bird-king appears, shaking the earth with his wings.
source_excerpt: in order to terrify the kings and display his own prowess he thought of the highly powerful son of Vinatā ... As soon as he was thought of Vinatā's son, assuming a form that could be seen easily, approached Keshava.

title: Jarasandha Warns the Kings
one_line_summary: At Bhishmaka's council Jarasandha warns the assembled kings that Krishna is Vishnu himself, whose arrival for the maiden spells calamity; Sunitha concurs.
source_excerpt: This Krishna ... has come here for the maiden and forsooth he will set forth mighty exertions for acquiring her. ... Forsooth I tell you that Vishnu himself has come for this Swayamvara.

title: The Kings Debate and Bhishmaka Yields
one_line_summary: Dantavakra urges peace with Krishna while Salwa scorns fear; Bhishmaka, fearing for his arrogant son Rukmi, resolves to go and propitiate Krishna.
source_excerpt: Dantavakra said: ... 'let us go and offer the high-souled Keshava hospitality ... if we make peace with Keshava we shall be able to live freed from anxiety and fear.' ... Bhismaka felt a desire to go to eternal Krishna for propitiating him.

title: Kaishika Offers His Kingdom
one_line_summary: The Vidarbha kings Kratha and Kaishika offer Krishna their kingdom and arrange his consecration, while a celestial voice announces that Indra has sent a golden seat.
source_excerpt: the two heroic and noble kings of Vidarbha, said: 'Blessed is our birth and fame to-day ... We now install thee in our kingdom.' ... 'For him the king of gods has sent this white seat of gold ... Do thou along with other kings place him on this seat and sprinkle him.'

title: Krishna's Royal Consecration
one_line_summary: Before the assembled kings, celestial jars pour sacred water and Indra himself adorns Krishna, completing the Abhisheka ceremony of his imperial consecration.
source_excerpt: from the sky, celestial jars ... began to pour down, like clouds, water mixed with gold, gems, flowers and scented powders on the occasion of the ceremony of his royal unction. ... Having performed duly according to rites, the Abhisheka ceremony of Janārddana, before the very presence of the kings.

title: Krishna Reveals Rukmini Is Lakshmi
one_line_summary: In dialogue with Bhishmaka, Krishna declares that Rukmini is the goddess Lakshmi born to be his wife and should not be given away in a public swayamvara.
source_excerpt: Krishna said: ... 'truly your daughter Rukshmini is not a woman; she is the very goddess Sree. For some object and at the words of Brahmā she is born (as a woman). She should not be given away in a Swayamvara where all the kings will be assembled.'

title: Krishna Departs and Bhishmaka Beholds His Cosmic Form
one_line_summary: Krishna takes leave of Bhishmaka, who beholds his universal form of a thousand heads and arms and worships him with a eulogy before the kings follow him out.
source_excerpt: beholding the prime and self-sprung Krishna, having eyes like red lotuses, thousand feet, thousand eyes, thousand arms ... the king Bhishmaka bowed unto him and began to eulogise his glories.

title: Shalya Proposes Inviting Kalayavana
one_line_summary: Shalya tells the kings that Kalayavana, whom no prince of Mathura can slay by Rudra's boon, should be invited against Krishna; Jarasandha dispatches Shalya as envoy.
source_excerpt: Shalya said: ... 'Kālayavana is incapable of being slain by Keshava. ... send an emissary to the capital of the king of Yavanas.' ... 'This effulgent king of Soubha ... let him proceed to the capital of Yavana.'

title: Rukmini Declares She Weds Only Krishna
one_line_summary: After the kings disperse, Rukmini tells her friends that she will accept no husband but the lotus-eyed Krishna.
source_excerpt: the chaste and wise Rukshmini approached her friends and with her face bent down in shame said:—'I tell you truly, I do not wish to be the spouse of any body else save Krishna having lotus eyes.'

title: Shalya Delivers Jarasandha's Message
one_line_summary: Shalya arrives at Kalayavana's court, recounts the destruction at Gomanta and Jarasandha's plea, and urges Kalayavana to march on Mathura.
source_excerpt: Shalya said:—O king of Yavanas, hear I shall describe at length what the king of Magadha has deputed me to communicate to you. ... 'enter the city of Mathurā with your army establish your glory there.'

title: Kalayavana Marches on Mathura
one_line_summary: Kalayavana, elated by the kings' request, honors Shalya and sets out that very day with his army to vanquish Krishna.
source_excerpt: Kalayavana said: ... 'in this auspicious moment I shall even to-day start for Mathurā for defeating Keshava in the battle-field.' ... he set out with his army for vanquishing Janārddana.

title: Ugrasena Welcomes Krishna Back
one_line_summary: Krishna returns to Mathura, where Ugrasena comes out to honor him; Krishna declines the royal arghya and reaffirms Ugrasena as king, then consoles him over Kamsa's death.
source_excerpt: Krishna ... said:—'O king of Mathurā, while I have installed you, declaring, Be you the lord of Mathura, it does not behove me to make it otherwise. ... get upon your white car ... govern the city of Mathurā, delightedly with your sons and grand-sons.'

title: Garuda Reports the Site of Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Garuda returns from reconnoitering Kushasthali and praises it as a fitting abode; Krishna, knowing Jarasandha unslayable, resolves to leave Mathura.
source_excerpt: Krishna ... said:—'O Vinatā's son, the king Jarāsandha is unslayable by us. ... it never bodes good for us to live in this city of Mathura.' ... Garuda said: ... 'thy city will be celebrated in the three worlds under the name of Dwāravati.'

title: Krishna Proposes Leaving Mathura
one_line_summary: Krishna counsels the Yadavas that Mathura is too small and exposed, and they agree to leave; the Yadava host sets out westward toward the ocean.
source_excerpt: the lotus-eyed Krishna addressed the following reasonable words to the Yadus in their assembly:—'This Mathurā city is the abode of the Yadus ... the city of Mathurā is very limited and the enemies can easily enter it. ... it is better that we should live elsewhere.'

title: Krishna Selects the Site of Dwaraka
one_line_summary: The Yadavas reach the ocean shore, and Krishna, seeking a place to build, chooses the coppery tract near Mount Raivata where the Yadavas encamp.
source_excerpt: Searching for a site where he would lay out a city Krishna ... saw an extensive tract of land situated on the bank of the ocean. ... Keshava selected that site for his city and the Yādavas also wanted to encamp their soldiers there.

title: The Serpent-Jar Stratagem
one_line_summary: As Kalayavana advances, Krishna sends him a sealed jar holding a black serpent as a warning; Kalayavana answers by filling the jar with ants that devour it.
source_excerpt: Keshava sent an envoy to the king of Yavanas. In order to terrorize him ... put a highly dreadful black serpent ... into a jar and sealed it up. ... understanding that the Yadavas had sent it to terrorize him Kalayavana filled that jar with dreadful ants.

title: Kalayavana Burned by Muchukunda
one_line_summary: Fleeing on foot, Krishna lures Kalayavana into the cave of the sleeping king Muchukunda, who wakes and reduces the Yavana king to ashes with his enraged gaze.
source_excerpt: when pursued by his Mlechcha enemy he humbly entered into Muchukunda's cave. ... With the touch of the foot the royal saint Muchukunda awoke ... he looked at the Yavana king with angry eyes. As soon as he was eyed, the king of Yavanas was all ablaze.

title: Viswakarma Builds Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Krishna summons the divine architect Viswakarma, and after the ocean withdraws twelve yojanas, the celestial city of Dwaravati is raised.
source_excerpt: Krishna ... thought of Viswakarmā, in his mind, so that he might come there. ... 'O ocean, if you have any respect for me, then withdraw thy form in the water extending over twelve yojanas.' ... by Viswakarma's mental effort that beautiful Vaishnava city, by name Dwarkāvati, was built.

title: Krishna Enriches Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Krishna bids the treasure-guard Sankha shower wealth on every household and sends Vayu to fetch the celestial assembly-hall Sudharma from heaven.
source_excerpt: Krishna ... felt a desire of gratifying his own people, who were poor, with profuse riches. ... Sankha ... ordered them to shower heaps of wealth in every house of Dwāravati. ... 'beg of them the assembly Hall Sudharmā and bring it to Dwarkā.'
variant_notes: VARIANT of the Sudharman-hall motif: Harivamsha 1.115 includes the hall in Dwaraka's enrichment; Vishnu Purana 5.21 narrates the hall separately for Ugrasena at Mathura. Different placement — kept separate.

title: Baladeva Marries Revati
one_line_summary: Some days after the founding of Dwaraka, Baladeva weds Revati, the daughter of king Revata, with Rishabha's consent.
source_excerpt: A few days after with Reshava's consent Baladeva acquired the good-natured daughter of Revata, by name Revati.

title: Rukmi Attacks and Is Defeated
one_line_summary: Rukmi vows to slay Krishna for carrying off his sister, but in the duel near the Narmada Krishna breaks his bow and car, and only spares him at Rukmini's plea.
source_excerpt: Hearing that his sister had been carried away by Krishna Rukshmi, filled with anger, promised ... 'I shall not return to the city of Kundina without slaying Krishna and bringing back Rukshmini.' ... Beholding her brother lying down motionless on earth, Rukshmini, for his life, fell at Vishnu's feet.

title: Krishna Weds Rukmini
one_line_summary: Returning to Dwaraka, Krishna duly espouses Rukmini, who becomes his first wife and bears ten sons; his other marriages are briefly enumerated.
source_excerpt: When Rāma, with the Vrishni army, arrived at Dwārakā the powerful Keshavā duly espoused Rukshmini. ... The powerful Mādhava begat on her ten sons—all mighty car-warriors, namely the highly powerful Pradyumna ...

title: Rukmavati's Swayamvara and Marriage
one_line_summary: Rukmi's daughter Rukmavati chooses Pradyumna at her swayamvara; later her son Aniruddha is wed to Rukmavati's namesake, the granddaughter of Rukmi.
source_excerpt: the Bidarbha king's daughter chose Pradyumna the slayer of enemies (for her husband). ... 'I confer Rukshmavati on Aniruddha endued with accomplishments and of a peaceful nature.'

title: Balarama Kills Rukmi at Dice
one_line_summary: At Aniruddha's wedding feast, Rukmi cheats Balarama at dice and mocks him; enraged, Balarama slays Rukmi with the dice-board and breaks the Kalinga king's teeth.
source_excerpt: In that game of dice with Rukshmi, Baladeva betted from ten to a thousand gold coins. ... Enraged at those words, Rāma, the foremost of Yadus, slew with force that harsh-speeched and jealous Rukshmi. ... he struck down the teeth of the Kalinga king.

title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura to Free Shamva
one_line_summary: Recounting Balarama's deeds, Vaishampayana tells how Balarama, to free the imprisoned Shamva, hooked his ploughshare into Hastinapura and threatened to fling the city into the Ganges.
source_excerpt: Hearing of his confinement the highly powerful Rāma went to that city for releasing him ... taking up his invincible ... weapon, plough-share ... and fixing it on the wall of the city he thought of, throwing that city of the Kauravas into the Ganges. Beholding his city thus whirled the king Duryodhana sent Shamva with his wife to the highly powerful Rāma.
notes: Retrospective recital of Balarama's deeds given in answer to Janamejaya; framed as past history rather than present narrative.

title: Indra Seeks Krishna's Help Against Naraka
one_line_summary: Indra descends to Dwaraka, recounts how the demon Naraka stole Aditi's ear-rings, and asks Krishna to slay him; Krishna departs with Satyabhama on Garuda.
source_excerpt: Indra ... said: 'Elated with the boon conferred on him by Brahmā the great Asura Naraka has foolishly stolen the ear-rings of Aditi. ... Do thou therefore kill that sinful wretch.' ... he, along with Satyabhāmā, sat on Garuda's back and immediately started with Sakra.

title: Krishna Slays Naraka
one_line_summary: Krishna battles and kills Naraka's generals Muru, Nisunda, Hayagriva and Panchajana, then cuts the demon Naraka in two with his discus.
source_excerpt: Fighting with Naraka for a moment the dreadful Janārddana cut him into two pieces with his effulgent discus. ... Beholding his son slain, Bhumi came with the pair of Kundalas to Govinda.

title: Krishna Frees the Captive Maidens
one_line_summary: Krishna seizes Naraka's treasure and frees the sixteen thousand captive maidens, who choose him as their husband and are carried to Dwaraka.
source_excerpt: Having arrived at the Treasury of Naraka, Janārdana saw there, diamonds, pearls, corals, sapphires, emeralds ... Taking himself the Varuni umbrella capable of showering gold, he rode Garuda ... Having thus welcome[d] those lotus eyed damsels ... took them all to Dwāraka.

title: Krishna Returns Aditi's Ear-rings and Uproots the Parijata
one_line_summary: Krishna travels to heaven, restores Aditi's ear-rings and receives her blessing, then forcibly uproots the celestial Parijata tree and carries it off on Garuda.
source_excerpt: Giving to the king of gods the pair of ear-rings belonging to Aditi and saluting him ... Aditi was pleased and took up her two sons on her lap. ... Krishna of unlimited powers, forcibly up-rooted it [the Pārijata] and placed it on Garuda's head.
notes: The Parijata uprooting seeds the ensuing Satyabhama-Indra conflict (chs 122-127).

title: Narada Presents the Parijata Flower to Rukmini
one_line_summary: Narada gives Krishna a Parijata flower, which Krishna passes to Rukmini; the sage extols Rukmini as the foremost of his wives.
source_excerpt: Nārada ... gave him a Pārijata flower. ... Bhoja's daughter Rukshmini was by him, so Hari gave her that Parijata flower. ... 'among the sixteen thousand wives of Vāsudeva, I consider thee as the foremost and the most beloved.'

title: Satyabhama Is Consumed by Jealousy
one_line_summary: Satyabhama's maids report Rukmini's good fortune; the proud queen, unable to bear her co-wife's honor, casts off her ornaments and retires to the apartment of anger.
source_excerpt: But the highly proud Satyabhāma ... could not bear the accession of such a good fortune unto the other wife of her husband. ... Worked up with anger like the flame of fire ... she entered into the lonely apartment of anger.

title: Krishna Consoles the Jealous Satyabhama
one_line_summary: Krishna steals into Satyabhama's chamber and, fanning her and wiping her tears, protests that his love dwells in her alone.
source_excerpt: he approached Satyabhama with faltering steps. Taking up the fan and standing by her side, he then began to fan slowly ... 'Just as flame is in fire ... so my love resides in thee and thee only.'

title: Krishna Promises Satyabhama the Parijata Tree
one_line_summary: Satyabhama confesses her grief over the Parijata flower given to Rukmini; Krishna vows to fetch the whole Parijata tree from Indra's heaven for her.
source_excerpt: Krishna ... said: ... 'What to speak of a single flower, I shall fetch that best of all trees namely the Parijata tree itself, from the gardens of paradise, and keep it in thy mansion.' ... 'so be it, then; this shall be my foremost concern.'

title: Krishna Sends Narada to Ask Indra for the Parijata
one_line_summary: Krishna asks Narada to request the Parijata tree from Indra as a brotherly favour, and warns that if refused he will come himself to seize it.
source_excerpt: Krishna ... said: ... 'remind Pakasasana of all our ancient brotherly love ... Ask him therefore to send down to Dwarvati that best of all trees the Pārijāta.' ... 'If that lord of the immortals do not give the Parijata tree at thy request, I shall then hurl my mace at his breast.'

title: Indra Refuses and Challenges Krishna
one_line_summary: Narada relays Krishna's demand; Indra, recounting past grievances, refuses to part with the Parijata tree unless conquered in battle and sends back a challenge.
source_excerpt: Indra ... said: ... 'Until I am conquered in a battle by the wielder of the discus Krishna, I will not, O foremost of sages, part with the Pārijata tree.' ... 'tell Achyuta that I am prepared for the quarrel.'
